Class KonceptGlossaryTreeprocessor

java.lang.Object
org.asciidoctor.extension.BaseProcessor
org.asciidoctor.extension.Treeprocessor
network.ike.docs.koncept.KonceptGlossaryTreeprocessor
All Implemented Interfaces:
org.asciidoctor.extension.Processor
public final class KonceptGlossaryTreeprocessor extends org.asciidoctor.extension.Treeprocessor
Builds a real, TOC-visible AST section for the comprehensive (koncept-glossary-all) glossary mode (IKE-Network/ike-issues#877).

KonceptGlossaryProcessor — the pre-existing, referenced-only (default) glossary — is a Postprocessor: it runs after conversion, injecting the whole glossary as a raw HTML string appended to the output. Asciidoctor's own table of contents is built from the parsed AST during conversion, before a postprocessor ever runs, so that glossary is structurally invisible to the TOC no matter how its content is grouped — the root cause of an 88-page guide with a single TOC entry.

This treeprocessor runs during tree processing instead, so the Section nodes it creates here are exactly what Asciidoctor's TOC-builder walks moments later. Two shapes, both covering every known koncept (from KonceptDefinitionSource.identifiers()):

  • Default — one flat "Koncept Glossary" section, alphabetical by label: a traditional glossary appendix. The intended companion to a hand-authored manuscript (separate chapters) that carries the narrative structure a reader actually wants — this treeprocessor's job is just comprehensive lookup, not organization.
  • koncept-glossary-grouped (set alongside koncept-glossary-all) — the original grouped shape: one child section per section field (computed against the live knowledge base by KonceptExtractor in tinkar-core, not derived here), titled with its group's own koncept label when the group is a genuine taxonomy subtree, opening with that koncept's own definition as the section's narrative. Kept as an opt-in for whoever wants taxonomy-shaped browsing instead of (or alongside, via a separate render) the flat default.

No-ops unless koncept-glossary-all is set, and skips the pdf (Prawn) and DocBook backends — the HTML5 family first; KonceptGlossaryProcessor keeps rendering the referenced-only (default) glossary for every backend, and keeps owning koncept-glossary-all for DocBook too (it never fully supported "all" there either — buildGlossaryDocbook always used the referenced-only registry — so this treeprocessor isn't ceding anything new).

Registered via SPI (KonceptExtensionRegistry) like FrontBackMatterTreeprocessor: a plain AST-only treeprocessor is safe for every backend, including Prawn — the backend guard below is a scope choice, not a crash-avoidance requirement.
